Explain node predictions

Source: R/graph-explain.R
explain.Rd

Post hoc explanations of a trained model's output for one target node (or one graph, with target = NULL and a graph level model). They describe how the model's output responds to its inputs; they are not causal explanations of the data generating process, and attention weights alone are not importance scores.

Usage

explain_saliency(model, g, target = NULL, output = NULL, times_input = FALSE)

explain_integrated_gradients(
  model,
  g,
  target = NULL,
  output = NULL,
  baseline = 0,
  steps = 50L
)

explain_edges(model, g, target = NULL, output = NULL)

explain_occlusion(model, g, target = NULL, output = NULL)

gnn_explainer(
  model,
  g,
  target = NULL,
  output = NULL,
  epochs = 100L,
  lr = 0.01,
  edge_size = 0.005,
  feature_size = 1,
  entropy = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A trained model (or a graph_fit).

g

A graph_data object.

target

Target node index, or NULL for a graph level output.

output

Output column to explain; default the predicted class.

times_input

Multiply gradients by the input.

baseline

Baseline features: a number or a matrix like g$x.

steps

Riemann sum points.

epochs

Optimization steps.

lr

Learning rate.

edge_size, feature_size

Sparsity penalties.

entropy

Mask entropy penalty, pushing mask values towards 0 or 1.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A list with attribution matrices or vectors and metadata, of class graph_explanation.

Details

  • explain_saliency(): gradient of the selected output with respect to node features (Simonyan et al. 2014), optionally times the input.

  • explain_integrated_gradients(): integrated gradients (Sundararajan et al. 2017) along a straight path from baseline to the features with a Riemann sum of steps points. The result includes completeness_gap, the difference between the summed attributions and f(x) - f(baseline); a large gap means more steps are needed.

  • explain_edges(): gradient of the output with respect to a multiplicative mask on edge weights, evaluated at mask 1. Needs a model whose layers use edge_weight ("gcn", "sage", "graph_conv", "gin").

  • explain_occlusion(): change in the output when each feature column, or each incoming edge of the target, is removed.

  • gnn_explainer(): learns a soft edge mask and feature mask that keep the prediction while staying sparse (Ying et al. 2019).

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  g <- split_nodes(dataset_karate(), seed = 1)
  fit <- train_graph_model(gnn_model("gcn", 34, 8, 2), g,
                           "node_classification", epochs = 20, seed = 1)
  ex <- explain_edges(fit, g, target = 1)
  head(ex$edges[order(-abs(ex$edges$attribution)), ])
}
#>    edge from to attribution
#> 22   22   13  1  0.03337903
#> 20   20   12  1  0.03144555
#> 19   19    1 12 -0.02480568
#> 30   30   22  1  0.02403817
#> 6     6    4  1  0.02362620
#> 32   32   32  1 -0.02206503
